claim.quote: While the Drell-Yan production exhibits the normal expected behaviour, the yield of J/ψ in Pb-Pb interactions is abnormally low, as it lies 9 standard deviations below the expected value.

name: NA50 anomalous J/psi suppression in Pb-Pb interactions
notes: Typed as an anomaly (abnormal suppression relative to normal nuclear absorption), not a discovery of quark-gluon plasma; the 1997 abstract does not make that claim.

significance.quote: as it lies 9 standard deviations below the expected value
significance.value: 9 standard deviations below the expected value

summary.plain: NA50 compared J/psi production in lead-lead collisions with what proton and light-ion data predicted. The Drell-Yan process behaved normally, but the J/psi yield was abnormally low, 9 standard deviations below the expectation, and more so in central collisions: the anomalous J/psi suppression.
summary.technical: Comparison of the Drell-Yan and J/psi cross sections in Pb-Pb at 158 GeV/c per nucleon with values extrapolated from proton and light-ion reactions: normal Drell-Yan, but J/psi abnormally low (9 sigma below the expected value) with a departure growing from peripheral to central collisions.

title: Anomalous J/ψ suppression in Pb-Pb interactions at 158 GeV/c per nucleon
why_it_matters: The suppression of the J/psi was predicted as a signature of quark-gluon plasma, so the anomalous suppression was a key piece of the evidence CERN announced in February 2000.
